arxiv-2201-08598.creator: I.Irina Nikishinalabel=e1]irina.nikishina@skoltech.ru, M.Mikhail Tikhomirovlabel=e3]tikhomirov.mm@gmail.com, L.Varvara Logachevalabel=e2]v.logacheva@skoltech.ru, Y.Yuriy Nazarovlabel=e4]nazarov.yuriy.pavlovich@gmail.com, A.Alexander Panchenkolabel=e5]a.panchenko@skoltech.ru, N.Natalia Loukachevitchl
arxiv-2201-08598.description: Abstract Knowledge graphs such as DBpedia, Freebase or Wikidata always contain a taxonomic backbone that allows the arrangement and structuring of various concepts in accordance with hypo-hypernym (“class-subclass”) relationship. With the rapid growth of lexical resources for specific domains, the problem of automatic extension of the existing knowledge bases with new words is becoming more and more widespread.

arxiv-2211-12060.description: Abstract We report a search for a heavier partner of the recently observed Z c ​ s ​ ( 3985 ) − Z_{cs}(3985)^{-} state, denoted as Z c ​ s ′ ⁣ − Z_{cs}^{\prime-} , in the process e + ​ e − → K + ​ D s ∗ ⁣ − ​ D ∗ 0 + c .

arxiv-2303-13531.title: Discovering Hierarchical Process Models: an Approach Based on Events Clustering Thanks: This work is supported by the Basic Research Program at HSE University, Russia.
arxiv-2303-13531.creator: Antonina K. Begicheva, Irina A. Lomazova, Roman A. Nesterov
arxiv-2303-13531.description: Abstract Process mining is a field of computer science that deals with discovery and analysis of process models based on automatically generated event logs. Currently, many companies use this technology for optimization and improving their processes. However, a discovered process model may be too detailed, sophisticated and difficult for experts to understand.

arxiv-2306-05209.title: Multiplication of the orbital angular momentum of phonon polaritons via sublinear dispersion
arxiv-2306-05209.creator: Andrea Mancini, Lin Nan, Rodrigo Berté, Emiliano Cortés, Haoran Ren, Stefan A. Maier
arxiv-2306-05209.description: Abstract Optical vortices (OVs) promise to greatly enhance optical information capacity via orbital angular momentum (OAM) multiplexing. The need for on-chip integration of OAM technologies has prompted research into subwavelength-confined polaritonic OVs. However, the topological order imprinted by the structure used for the transduction from free-space beams to surface polaritons is inherently fixed after fabrication.

arxiv-2309-07208.title: Tilted Dark Halos are Common, Long-Lived, and can Warp Galactic Disks
arxiv-2309-07208.creator: Jiwon Jesse Han, Vadim Semenov, Charlie Conroy, Lars Hernquist
arxiv-2309-07208.description: Abstract In the Λ \Lambda -CDM paradigm, the dark halo governs the gravitational potential within which a galaxy can form and evolve. In this Letter we show that the present-day inner ( r < 50 ​ kpc r<50\text{ kpc} ) dark halo can be significantly misaligned with the stellar disk.

arxiv-2311-12128.title: Fingerspelling PoseNet: Enhancing Fingerspelling Translation with Pose-Based Transformer Models
arxiv-2311-12128.creator: Pooya Fayyazsanavi, Negar Nejatishahidin, Jana Košecká
arxiv-2311-12128.description: Abstract We address the task of American Sign Language fingerspelling translation using videos in the wild. We exploit advances in more accurate hand pose estimation and propose a novel architecture that leverages the transformer based encoder-decoder model enabling seamless contextual word translation.

arxiv-2311-15006.title: A Survey Examining Neuromorphic Architecture in Space and Challenges from Radiation Thanks: *Corresponding author
arxiv-2311-15006.creator: Jonathan Naoukin*, Murat Isik, Karn Tiwari
arxiv-2311-15006.description: Abstract Inspired by the human brain’s structure and function, neuromorphic computing has emerged as a promising approach for developing energy-efficient and powerful computing systems. Neuromorphic computing offers significant processing speed and power consumption advantages in aerospace applications. These two factors are crucial for real-time data analysis and decision-making.

arxiv-2401-00369.title: Analysis of biologically plausible neuron models for regression with spiking neural networks Thanks: This work was supported by the Vannevar Bush Faculty Fellowship award (GEK) from ONR (N00014-22-1-2795). The work of GEK is supported by the U.S. Department of Energy, Advanced Scientific Computing R
arxiv-2401-00369.creator: Mario De Florio, Adar Kahana, George Em Karniadakis
arxiv-2401-00369.description: Abstract This paper explores the impact of biologically plausible neuron models on the performance of Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) for regression tasks. While SNNs are widely recognized for classification tasks, their application to Scientific Machine Learning and regression remains underexplored. We focus on the membrane component of SNNs, comparing four neuron models: Leaky Integrate-and-Fire, FitzHugh–Nagumo, Izhikevich, and Hodgkin-Huxley.

arxiv-2408-13687.title: Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold
arxiv-2408-13687.creator: Google Quantum AI and Collaborators
arxiv-2408-13687.description: Abstract Quantum error correction [ 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 ] provides a path to reach practical quantum computing by combining multiple physical qubits into a logical qubit, where the logical error rate is suppressed exponentially as more qubits are added. However, this exponential suppression only occurs if the physical error rate is below a critical threshold.

arxiv-2411-10442.title: Enhancing the Reasoning Ability of Multimodal Large Language Models via Mixed Preference Optimization
arxiv-2411-10442.creator: Weiyun Wang, Zhe Chen, Wenhai Wang, Yue Cao, Yangzhou Liu, Zhangwei Gao, Jinguo Zhu, Xizhou Zhu, Lewei Lu, Yu Qiao, Jifeng Dai
arxiv-2411-10442.description: Abstract Existing open-source multimodal large language models (MLLMs) generally follow a training process involving pre-training and supervised fine-tuning. However, these models suffer from distribution shifts, which limit their multimodal reasoning, particularly in the Chain-of-Thought (CoT) performance. To address this, we introduce a preference optimization (PO) process to enhance the multimodal reasoning capabilities of MLLMs.

arxiv-2503-07752.title: Neutrino masses and mixing: Entering the era of subpercent precision
arxiv-2503-07752.creator: Francesco Capozzi, William Giarè, Eligio Lisi, Antonio Marrone, Alessandro Melchiorri, Antonio Palazzo
arxiv-2503-07752.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Francesco Capozzi, William Giarè, Eligio Lisi, Antonio Marrone, Alessandro Melchiorri, Antonio Palazzo. We perform an updated global analysis of the known and unknown parameters of the standard 3 ​ ν 3\nu framework, using data available at the beginning of 2025.

arxiv-2503-19755.title: ORION: A Holistic End-to-End Autonomous Driving Framework by Vision-Language Instructed Action Generation
arxiv-2503-19755.creator: Haoyu Fu, Diankun Zhang, Zongchuang Zhao, Jianfeng Cui, Dingkang Liang, Chong Zhang, Dingyuan Zhang, Hongwei Xie, Bing Wang, Xiang Bai
arxiv-2503-19755.description: Abstract End-to-end (E2E) autonomous driving methods still struggle to make correct decisions in interactive closed-loop evaluation due to limited causal reasoning capability. Current methods attempt to leverage the powerful understanding and reasoning abilities of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to resolve this dilemma.

arxiv-2510-17739.title: Joint Multi-Condition Representation Modelling via Matrix Factorisation for Visual Place Recognition Thanks: *Corresponding author. Affiliation: Timur Ismagilov*, Shakaiba Majeed, Michael Milford, Tan Viet Tuyen Nguyen Thanks: Timur Ismagilov, Tan Viet Tuyen Nguyen, Sarvapali D. Ramchurn and Shoaib
arxiv-2510-17739.description: Abstract We address multi-reference visual place recognition (VPR), where reference sets captured under varying conditions are used to improve localisation performance. While deep learning with large-scale training improves robustness, increasing data diversity and model complexity incur extensive computational cost during training and deployment.

arxiv-2512-21109.title: Robust and Efficient MuJoCo-based Model Predictive Control via Web of Affine Spaces Derivatives
arxiv-2512-21109.creator: Chen Liang and Daniel Rakita
arxiv-2512-21109.description: Abstract MuJoCo is a powerful and efficient physics simulator widely used in robotics. One common way it is applied in practice is through Model Predictive Control (MPC), which uses repeated rollouts of the simulator to optimize future actions and generate responsive control policies in real time.

arxiv-2602-19520.title: Decomposing Crowd Wisdom: Domain-Specific Calibration Dynamics in Prediction Markets Thanks: Citation : Le, N.A. (2026). Decomposing Crowd Wisdom: Domain-Specific Calibration Dynamics in Prediction Markets. Preprint.
arxiv-2602-19520.creator: Nam Anh Le
arxiv-2602-19520.description: Abstract Prediction markets are increasingly used as probability forecasting tools, yet their usefulness depends on calibration, specifically whether a contract trading at 70 cents truly implies a 70% probability. Using 292 million trades across 327,000 binary contracts on Kalshi and Polymarket, this paper shows that calibration is a structured, multidimensional phenomenon.

pmc-10611346.title: Parallelized Particle Swarm Optimization on FPGA for Realtime Ballistic Target Tracking
pmc-10611346.creator: Juhyeon Park, Heoncheol Lee, Hyuck-Hoon Kwon, Yeji Hwang, Wonseok Choi
pmc-10611346.description: This paper addresses the problem of tracking a high-speed ballistic target in real time. Particle swarm optimization (PSO) can be a solution to overcome the motion of the ballistic target and the nonlinearity of the measurement model. However, in general, particle swarm optimization requires a great deal of computation time, so it is difficult to apply to realtime systems.

pmc-10740130.title: Advances in Bioelectrode Design for Developing Electrochemical Biosensors
pmc-10740130.creator: Nabajyoti Kalita, Sudarshan Gogoi, Shelley D. Minteer, Pranab Goswami
pmc-10740130.description: The critical performance factors such as selectivity, sensitivity, operational and storage stability, and response time of electrochemical biosensors are governed mainly by the function of their key component, the bioelectrode. Suitable design and fabrication strategies of the bioelectrode interface are essential for realizing the requisite performance of the biosensors for their practical utility.

pmc-11306186.title: Argonaute-2 autoantibodies: a promising biomarker for predicting mortality in HBV-related acute-on-chronic liver failure patients with cirrhosis
pmc-11306186.creator: Yixuan Wang, Yue Hu, Jiaqi Li, Huailu Ma, Zongqi Shi, Chaojing Wen, Yu Long, Ziwei Li, Hang Sun, Yixuan Yang, Xiaofeng Shi
pmc-11306186.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background & aimsHBV infection initiates autoimmune responses, leading to autoantibody generation. This research explores the role of autoantibodies in HBV-related Acute-on-Chronic Liver Failure (ACLF), offering novel perspectives for clinical management.MethodWe applied immunoprecipitation and iTRAQ techniques to screen for autoantibodies in serum from HBV-related cirrhosis patients and conducted detection with conformation- stabilizing ELISA in a cohort of 238 HBV-infected individuals and 49 health controls.

pmc-11511412.title: A Lipid Nanoparticle-Formulated Self-Amplifying RNA Rift Valley Fever Vaccine Induces a Robust Humoral Immune Response in Mice
pmc-11511412.creator: Paul K Kitandwe, Paul Rogers, Kai Hu, Owen Nayebare, Anna K Blakney, Paul F McKay, Pontiano Kaleebu, Robin J Shattock, S Louise Cosby
pmc-11511412.description: Rift Valley fever (RVF) is a mosquito-borne viral zoonosis that causes high fetal and neonatal mortality rates in ruminants and sometimes severe to fatal complications like encephalitis and hemorrhagic fever in humans. There is no licensed RVF vaccine for human use while approved livestock vaccines have suboptimal safety or efficacy.

pmc-11642167.title: A Review of the Literature on Videoscopic and Robotic Inguinal–Iliac–Obturator Lymphadenectomy in Patients with Cutaneous Melanoma
pmc-11642167.creator: Matteo Matteucci, Paolo Bruzzone, Sabrina Pinto, Piero Covarelli, Carlo Boselli, Georgi I. Popivanov, Roberto Cirocchi
pmc-11642167.description: Inguinal–iliac–obturator lymph node dissection is essential in the treatment of patients with cutaneous melanoma exhibiting the clinical or radiological involvement of pelvic lymph nodes. The open procedure is associated with elevated mortality rates. Numerous minimally invasive approaches have been suggested to mitigate the impact of this surgery on the patient’s quality of life.

pmc-12470080.title: RNA Polymerase I Dysfunction Underlying Craniofacial Syndromes: Integrated Genetic Analysis Reveals Parallels to 22q11.2 Deletion Syndrome
pmc-12470080.creator: Spencer Silvey, Scott Lovell, Merlin G. Butler
pmc-12470080.description: Background/Objective: POLR1A and related gene variants cause craniofacial and developmental syndromes, including Acrofacial Dysostosis-Cincinnati, Treacher-Collins types 2–4, and TWIST1-associated disorders. Using a patient case integrated with molecular analyses, we aimed to clarify shared pathogenic mechanisms and propose these conditions as part of a spectrum of RNA polymerase I (Pol I)–related ribosomopathies.

pmc-12607310.title: The Constructional Approach to Zoo Animal Training: Enhancing Welfare Through Emerging Evidence-Based Behavioral Science
pmc-12607310.creator: Barbara Heidenreich, Annette Pedersen, Oriol Talló-Parra, Xavier Manteca
pmc-12607310.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Simple SummaryAnimal welfare has become a cornerstone of modern zoo and aquarium animal care practices. This article introduces the constructional approach to animal training as a practical, emerging evidence-based method that can improve zoo animal welfare. Unlike traditional training approaches that focus on eliminating problem behaviors, the constructional approach emphasizes building desirable behaviors, providing animals with genuine choices, and understanding their emotional welfare through analyzing contingencies.

pmc-12659065.title: Enrichment of vitamin B12-producing Porphyrobacter in the phycosphere microbiome promotes microalgal stress adaptation to antibiotic exposure
pmc-12659065.creator: Qilu Cheng, Junwei Ma, Yuyi Yang, Jinchuan Ma, Hans-Peter Grossart, Ligen Xu, Hui Lin
pmc-12659065.description: BackgroundPlanktonic microalgae deploy multifaceted responsive and adaptive strategies against anthropogenic pollutants; however, current understanding of antibiotic resistance mechanisms remains predominantly focused on intrinsic physiological adaptations. While microalgae maintain intimate relationships with the phycosphere microbiome, the ecological roles of these associated microbes in mediating host adaptation to polluted environments are inadequately characterized.

pmc-13058601.title: Two new species of Comesomatidae (Nematoda, Araeolaimida) from the Rizhao coast of the Yellow Sea, China
pmc-13058601.creator: Huiying Yu, Chunming Wang
pmc-13058601.description: To study the diversity and taxonomy of marine nematodes on the Rizhao coast, undisturbed sediment samples have been systematically collected since 2022. pmc-13388546.title: Comprehensive genomic analysis of five kindreds with multiple childhood leukemias: importance of individual functional analysis for rare ETV6 germline variants

Nevertheless, the rare variants identified in diagnostic samples may be misinterpreted without variant-level functional evaluation and cautious clinical interpretation. pmc-13576163.creator: Margaret Gatz, Wendy J. Mack, Daniel Eid Rodriguez, Raul Quispe Gutierrez, Jesus Bani Cuata, Helena C. Chui, Ellen E. Walters, Daniel K. Cummings, Paul L. Hooper, Henrik Zetterberg, Caleb E. Finch, Benjamin C. Trumble, Jonathan Stieglitz, Michael D. Gurven, Randall C. Thompson, Gregory S. Thomas, Th
pmc-13576163.description: INTRODUCTIONWe studied dementia incidence and risk factors in Indigenous Tsimane and Moseten Amerindian populations in Amazonian Bolivia with largely subsistence lifestyles.METHODSA median of 4.7 years after baseline dementia assessment, 730 participants (52% male; mean age 67.3 years) were re‐visited at two follow‐up phases to determine new cases among non‐demented at baseline. Clinical evaluation was adapted to culture, language, and illiteracy.

uslaw-usc-t7-s1339c.title: 7 U.S.C. § 1339c — Feed grains diversion programs for 1964 and subsequent years; feed grain acreage considered wheat acreage and wheat acreage considered feed grain acreage
uslaw-usc-t7-s1339c.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t7-s1339c.description: United States Code, Title 7 (Agriculture); Chapter 35 (Agricultural Adjustment Act Of 1938); Subchapter II (Loans, Parity Payments, Consumer Safeguards, Marketing Quotas, And Marketing Certificates); Part B (Marketing Quotas); Subpart iii (Marketing Quotas—Wheat). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Effective with the 1964 crop, during any year in which an acreage diversion program is in effect for feed grains, the Secretary shall, notwithstanding.
